story.title: Aisha Wahab Wins Special Election for California's 14th Congressional District
story.summary: Aisha Wahab has won the special election to fill the remainder of Eric Swalwell's term in California's 14th Congressional District. Wahab, a state senator, defeated fellow Democrat Melissa Hernandez. This victory makes her the first Afghan American elected to Congress. The partial term will conclude in January 2027, after which a new candidate will be elected for the full term in November.

explore_lenses.label: What changes before the new Congress begins?
explore_lenses.title: A short-term House replacement
explore_lenses.summary: The special election fills the vacancy created by Eric Swalwell’s April resignation, rather than deciding the district’s next full two-year representative term.

claims.text: Gov. Gavin Newsom’s proclamation set the August 18, 2026 special election specifically to fill the House vacancy resulting from Swalwell’s resignation.
AP reports that Wahab will serve the remainder of the term ending in January 2027 and will be the first Afghan American to serve in Congress.

As of August 21, the California Secretary of State’s CD-14 page lists the August 18 special general election but does not yet link final official results, so the timing of formal certification and Wahab’s swearing-in is not stated there.

explore_lenses.label: What separated Wahab and Hernandez?
explore_lenses.title: Policy and outside-money disputes
explore_lenses.summary: Although both finalists were Democrats, the campaign featured documented differences over immigration enforcement and Gaza, as well as a dispute over outside spending.

claims.text: At an April forum, Wahab said yes when asked whether what was happening to Palestinians constituted genocide; Hernandez said Israel had a right to defend itself after Hamas’ October 2023 attack but that destruction in Gaza had gone too far.

El País reported that both candidates supported a citizenship path for undocumented immigrants and criticized ICE raids, but Wahab favored abolishing ICE while Hernandez advocated fundamental reform of the agency.

AP reported that groups affiliated with AIPAC spent millions supporting Hernandez and opposing Wahab; Wahab argued that the district could not be bought, while Hernandez said she had run a competitive race and had not given up.

explore_lenses.label: Why will voters decide the seat again in November?
explore_lenses.title: A rematch for a full term
explore_lenses.summary: The August contest concerned only the unexpired term. Wahab and Hernandez are scheduled to face each other again for the next regular House term.

claims.text: AP reports that Wahab and Hernandez will meet again in a separate November election for the next full two-year term.
CBS reported that the November 3 general election will decide the next full term, with early voting and vote-by-mail beginning October 5.
Hernandez said the redrawn November district includes 26,000 more voters and predicted that her base in Dublin could improve her position in the rematch.

story_report.summary: Aisha Wahab defeated fellow Democrat Melissa Hernandez in California’s 14th Congressional District special election, winning the seat for the remainder of former Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. Wahab will serve through January 2027 and is the first Afghan American elected to Congress. The contest filled a vacancy created by Swalwell’s resignation; voters will separately choose a representative for the next full two-year term in a November election, where Wahab and Hernandez are set for a rematch.

sections.heading: Candidates Differed on Gaza and ICE
sections.body: The Democratic candidates offered different positions on Gaza and immigration enforcement. At an April forum, Wahab said she believed Palestinians were experiencing genocide, while Hernandez said Israel had the right to defend itself after Hamas’ October 2023 attack but that the destruction in Gaza had gone too far. Both supported a path to citizenship for undocumented immigrants and criticized ICE raids, but Wahab favored abolishing ICE while Hernandez backed fundamental reform. Groups affiliated with AIPAC spent millions supporting Hernandez and opposing Wahab, though reporting does not establish that the spending caused the result.

sections.heading: November Rematch Will Decide Full Term
sections.body: The November 3 general election will determine who holds the district’s next full two-year term, with early voting and vote-by-mail scheduled to begin October 5. Hernandez said the redrawn November district has 26,000 more voters and predicted that her base in Dublin could improve her position. That forecast remains untested: the special-election result does not decide the November contest.

unresolved.text: The available official state election page did not state when the result would be formally certified or when Wahab would be sworn into the House.

related_stories.title: Personalized mRNA Cancer Treatment Shows Promise Against Melanoma in Trial
related_stories.summary: Merck and Moderna announced that their personalized mRNA cancer treatment has successfully reduced melanoma tumor recurrence in a late-stage clinical trial. This marks a significant milestone in cancer treatment, as it is the first time an mRNA-based drug has shown positive results in such a large trial. Researchers are optimistic about the potential for this approach to be applied to other types of cancer in the future.

related_stories.title: Spain Relocates Migrants from Ceuta Beach to Shelters Amid Ongoing Crisis
related_stories.summary: Spain has begun relocating hundreds of migrants from a makeshift camp on Ceuta's El Trampolín beach to temporary shelters. This action comes nearly three weeks after a mass border surge resulted in thousands of migrants living without adequate shelter in the North African enclave.

related_stories.title: New York Woman Charged with Terrorism for Alleged Capitol Bomb Plot
related_stories.summary: A 35-year-old woman has been charged with a terrorism offense for allegedly plotting to bomb the New York State Capitol. Jessica Bowie reportedly expressed a desire to destroy the Capitol buildings to an FBI informant, leading to her arrest in a sting operation. The charges are linked to her alleged support for the Islamic State (ISIS) group.

related_stories.title: University Suspends Academic Following Plagiarism Allegations Against Late Professor
related_stories.summary: Nathan Cofnas, an academic who accused the late Professor Jason Arday of plagiarism, has been suspended by Ghent University. The suspension follows an investigation into allegations of discrimination against Arday. Cofnas announced the investigation on social media.
